newsitem.title: UK: Human Solutions Plc plans chain of 17 'Fit Stops'.
newsitem.headline: Human Solutions Plc plans chain of 17 'Fit Stops'.

text.p: Human Solutions Group Plc said on Friday it plans to open 17 high-street gymnasiums in Britain, to be called Fit Stops, over three years.
The group said it will fund the development by raising one million stg through an offer of 3.3 million shares at 30 pence per share, capitalising the group at 3.0 million.

The company has also applied for a listing on the OFEX, or off-exchange market. British athlete Sally Gunnell, who has a 10 percent stake in the business, will spearhead a fitness programme for the group. The first Fit Stop will open this summer in Sutton, southern England.

Fitness is a huge potential market in Britain, with UK spending on fitness and health forecast to rise to 1.057 billion stg in the year 2000 up from 711 million stg in 1995. But eight in ten women and seven out of ten men take no regular exercise, said the company in a statement.
"Most are out of shape, many will be seriously unfit," it said. Nearly half the female population and more than half the male population are overweight, while 95 percent of diets fail.
"What makes the problem worse is that couch potatoes may have developed an allergy to gyms with alarming machines and over-developed body builders," said the group.
